questions.section: PART TWO: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (90 marks) - QUESTION 1 (STATISTICS)
questions.question:
The table below shows the number of absentees recorded each day of a month in a school.

a) Complete the table (4 marks)
   class   | frequency (f) | midpoint (x) | fx
   1 – 5   | 3             | 3            | 9
   6 – 10  | 5             | 8            | 40
   11 – 15 | 7             | ......       | ......
   16 – 20 | 6             | ......       | ......
   21 – 25 | 4             | ......       | ......
   Σf = ......              |              | Σfx = ......

b) Which is the modal class (1 marks)

c) Calculate the mean number of absentees (2 marks)

b) The end of a term marks of a pupil in 4 subjects are shown below
   57  55  62  52, if his mean is 56
   i) Complete the table below (2 marks)
      deviations (d)            | 1 | -1 | ... | ...
      absolute deviations |d|  | 1 | 1  | ... | ...
   ii) Calculate the absolute mean deviation of his marks (2 marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a) Completed table:
   11 – 15: x = 13, fx = 7 × 13 = 91
   16 – 20: x = 18, fx = 6 × 18 = 108
   21 – 25: x = 23, fx = 4 × 23 = 92
   Σf = 3 + 5 + 7 + 6 + 4 = 25
   Σfx = 9 + 40 + 91 + 108 + 92 = 340

b) Modal class: 11 – 15 (it has the highest frequency, 7)

c) Mean = Σfx / Σf = 340 / 25 = 13.6 absentees

b) (the second part is also lettered b in the paper)
   i) Deviations from the mean 56: 57 - 56 = 1; 55 - 56 = -1; 62 - 56 = 6; 52 - 56 = -4
      Absolute deviations: 1, 1, 6, 4
   ii) Absolute mean deviation = (1 + 1 + 6 + 4) / 4 = 12 / 4 = 3

questions.section: PART TWO: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (90 marks) - QUESTION 2 (GRAPHS IN PRACTICAL SITUATION)
questions.question:
Warsame cycles from home to the town. He has stopped for a tea. After tea, he cycles back to home. The travel graph below shows his journey.

a) At what time did he begin to cycle? (1 mark)

b) How many minutes did he rest? (1 mark)

c) How far was he from home at 3 pm? (1 mark)

d) How long did it take him to get back home? (1 mark)

e) Find his speed as he travels back to home? (2 marks)

questions.section: PART TWO: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (90 marks) - QUESTION 4 (DERIVATIVE)
questions.question:
a) Find the derivative of y = √(x⁵) (3 marks)

b) Differentiate y = 3/x² - 2/x - 7 (4 marks)

c) If y = (x + 2)⁵, find dy/dx (use chain rule). (3 marks)

d) Differentiate f(x) = e^(3x²) (2 marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a) y = √(x⁵) = x^(5/2)
   dy/dx = (5/2) x^(3/2)

b) y = 3x⁻² - 2x⁻¹ - 7
   dy/dx = -6x⁻³ + 2x⁻² = -6/x³ + 2/x²

c) Let u = x + 2, so y = u⁵
   dy/dx = (dy/du)(du/dx) = 5u⁴ × 1 = 5(x + 2)⁴

d) f(x) = e^(3x²), let u = 3x²
   f'(x) = e^(3x²) × 6x = 6x e^(3x²)

questions.section: PART TWO: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (90 marks) - QUESTION 5 (APPLICATION OF DIFFERENTIATION)
questions.question:
a) Find the gradient of y = x² + 3 at x = 2 (2 marks)

b) Find the equation of the tangent of y = x² + 3 at (2, 7) (3 marks)

c) Find the stationary points of the following curve y = 5 + 2x - x² and determine their types (4 marks)

d) A stone is thrown vertically upwards such that its height s meters above the ground after t seconds is given by s = 40t - 10t²
   Find:
   i) its height above the ground after 1 sec (2 marks)
   ii) its velocity after 1 sec (3 marks)
   iii) the vertical height it reached (3 marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a) dy/dx = 2x; at x = 2, gradient = 2(2) = 4

b) Gradient at (2, 7) is 4
   y - 7 = 4(x - 2)
   y = 4x - 1

c) dy/dx = 2 - 2x = 0, so x = 1
   y = 5 + 2(1) - 1² = 6, so the stationary point is (1, 6)
   d²y/dx² = -2 < 0, so (1, 6) is a maximum point

d)
   i) s = 40(1) - 10(1)² = 30 m
   ii) v = ds/dt = 40 - 20t; at t = 1, v = 20 m/s
   iii) At the highest point v = 0: 40 - 20t = 0, so t = 2 s
        s = 40(2) - 10(2)² = 80 - 40 = 40 m

questions.section: PART TWO: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (90 marks) - QUESTION 6 (INTEGRATION)
questions.question:
a) Integrate ∫ (4/x³) dx (3 marks)

b) Find ∫₁³ (4x³ - 6x + 2) dx (3 marks)

c) Find the area between the curve y = x² and the x-axis from x = 1 to x = 2 (3 marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a) ∫ 4x⁻³ dx = 4 × x⁻²/(-2) + c = -2x⁻² + c = -2/x² + c

b) ∫₁³ (4x³ - 6x + 2) dx = [x⁴ - 3x² + 2x] from 1 to 3
   = (81 - 27 + 6) - (1 - 3 + 2) = 60 - 0 = 60

c) Area = ∫₁² x² dx = [x³/3] from 1 to 2 = 8/3 - 1/3 = 7/3 square units (about 2.33)

questions.section: PART TWO: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (90 marks) - QUESTION 7 (PROBABILITY)
questions.question:
a) A six-sided die is rolled.
   i) Write the sample space (2 marks)
      S = { ........................ }
   ii) What is the probability that an even number appears? (2 marks)

b) In how many ways can you choose 5 out of 10 friends to invite to a dinner party? (3 marks)

c) How many different arrangements can be made from the letters of the word BERBERA? (3 marks)

d) Use binomial theorem to expand (x + y)⁶ (4 marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a)
   i) S = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}
   ii) Even numbers = {2, 4, 6}, so P(even) = 3/6 = 1/2

b) Order does not matter, so use combinations: 10C5 = 10! / (5! 5!) = 252 ways

c) BERBERA has 7 letters with B repeated 2 times, E 2 times, R 2 times and A once:
   7! / (2! 2! 2!) = 5040 / 8 = 630 arrangements

d) (x + y)⁶ = x⁶ + 6x⁵y + 15x⁴y² + 20x³y³ + 15x²y⁴ + 6xy⁵ + y⁶

questions.section: PART TWO: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (90 marks) - QUESTION 8 (COMPLEX NUMBERS)
questions.question:
a) Express √(-16/9) in terms of i (2 marks)

b) Find the product of (2 - 3i)(3 + 2i) (3 marks)

c) Represent the following complex numbers on the argand diagram below (4 marks)
   i) Z₁ = 3 + 2i
   ii) Z₂ = -3 + 4i

d) Find the argument and modulus of the following complex number Z = -3 - 3i (4 marks)

diagram.caption: Blank Argand diagram: a grid with the real axis (marked -3 to 4) and the imaginary axis (marked 1 to 4) on which the student plots Z1 and Z2.

questions.answer_guide:
a) √(-16/9) = √(16/9) × √(-1) = (4/3)i

b) (2 - 3i)(3 + 2i) = 6 + 4i - 9i - 6i²
   = 6 - 5i + 6 (since i² = -1)
   = 12 - 5i

c) Plot each number as a point (real part, imaginary part):
   i) Z₁ = 3 + 2i is the point (3, 2): 3 units right and 2 units up
   ii) Z₂ = -3 + 4i is the point (-3, 4): 3 units left and 4 units up

d) Z = -3 - 3i
   Modulus |Z| = √((-3)² + (-3)²) = √18 = 3√2 (about 4.24)
   Argument: the point (-3, -3) is in the third quadrant, reference angle = tan⁻¹(3/3) = 45°
   arg Z = 180° + 45° = 225° (equivalent to -135°, or 5π/4 radians)
